title: Checkpoint linking fails for non-ASCII filenames

verdict.rationale: The evidence shows getStagedFiles was changed to use native git diff for performance, and later to `--raw -z` for submodule handling. None of it mentions quoted non-ASCII paths or choosing to compare Git's display-quoted output with literal paths. The behaviour reported in the issue was never decided.

evidence.text:
fix: optimize prepare-commit-msg hook performance for large repos

Replace go-git's worktree.Status() with native `git diff --cached` in
getStagedFiles (constant time vs O(all files)), cache the staged files
list across sessions to eliminate redundant calls, and read prompt.txt
directly from the shadow branch tree instead of parsing the full
transcript in getLastPrompt.

Keep submodule gitlinks out of FilesTouched and staged overlap

A dirty submodule pointer reached FilesTouched through the unconditional
git-status merge at turn end. prepare-commit-msg then saw the staged
gitlink as a new file in FilesTouched and stamped a trailer, PostCommit
could not match it to anything, and the path never left FilesTouched,
keeping the session pending.

dropUntrackablePaths now also drops any path whose HEAD tree or index
entry has mode 160000 (the index covers a submodule added but not yet
committed), on the same routes as the ignore filter. getStagedFiles
switches from `git diff --cached --name-only -z` to `--raw -z` and skips
entries whose staged mode, or HEAD mode for a staged removal, is
160000; a rename or copy still reports its new path. Mode-based
detection is platform independent.

Tests use a real `git submodule add`: a moved submodule pointer stays
out of FilesTouched on the turn-end and task-record routes, and a staged
submodule add lists only .gitmodules as staged. A parser test covers
modify, add, delete, rename and the three gitlink cases.
